title: A transit light curve
caption: As the planet crosses its star it blocks a fraction (R_p/R_*)² of the light. A Jupiter (0.1 R☉) in front of a Sun-like star dims it by 1%; an Earth would dim it by only about 0.008%.
alt: Relative brightness against time: flat at 1, dipping by 1 percent for the duration of the transit with sloping ingress and egress, then back to 1.
description: Brightness relative to the star alone.
During the transit it falls to 0.99: a 1% dip, since (0.1)² = 0.01.
The sloping edges are ingress and egress, while the planet's disc is only partly in front of the star.
The time axis is illustrative; the depth is from the lesson.
